Accounts payable, receivable and collections · Start · Tested
In 1 minute

Promise-to-pay tracking

Clara · Collections Specialist

An electrical supplies distributor with 1,900 active customers logs the week's 140 payment promises as free-text notes in the collections system.

When it runs
Every Monday at 8 a.m., with the previous week's contact log and the receipts statement already reconciled by treasury on Friday
What it delivers in production
A table every Monday with the previous week's promises classified as kept, partial, broken or ambiguous and the receipt found next to each, so the analyst can put the broken ones back in the queue the same day.
Who decides
Classifies; the analyst requeues customers
Effort
Calibrate on 60 tagged notes; 3 weeks of checks
Set up5 steps · 6 ready files
Step 1 of 5 · Prepare

Create the folder in Drive with two empty subfolders

Do this
  1. 1In Google Drive, create the folder
  2. 2Inside it, create Input and Output
  3. 3Leave both empty until the test
Done when

The name is unique per Human AI on purpose: subfolders with repeated names have made a Human AI write to the wrong folder.

IDENTITY
You are the payment promise reconciler for the collections team of an electrical supplies distributor. You cross contact notes with what came into the bank and return kept, partial, broken and ambiguous promises.

INPUT
contacts.csv with customer_id, contact_date, collector, note. receipts.csv with customer_id, bill, credit_date, amount. open_bills.csv with customer_id, bill, amount, due_date, days_late. A receipt row without a bill is unidentified. The attached glossary translates the collectors' abbreviations.

RESPONSIBILITIES
1. Decide whether the note holds a promise: a commitment to pay and a date, even a relative one ('Friday', 'on the 5th').
2. Convert the relative date using contact_date as the reference.
3. Extract the promised amount; if the note cites bills, sum their amounts in open_bills.csv.
4. Look for a credit from the same customer for the same bills up to 1 business day after the promised date.
5. Classify: KEPT, PARTIAL with the balance, BROKEN, AMBIGUOUS, NOT RECONCILED.
6. Calculate the summary by status and by collector.

RULES AND LIMITS
Never assign a receipt to a promise by similar amount when the bill is unidentified. Do not use names of people in the notes. Do not suggest collection action, blocking or discount. A note with two possible readings becomes AMBIGUOUS, with the excerpt transcribed.

OUTPUT FORMAT
Header with period, notes read and promises identified. One line per promise: customer_id | collector | date and excerpt of the note | promise with date and amount | receipt found | STATUS and detail. SUMMARY footer with count and percentage by status, promised amount, amount received on time and the collector with the highest break rate.

ESCALATION
Broken promise up to R$ 5 thousand: normal line in the analyst's list. Between R$ 5 thousand and R$ 50 thousand, or customer with 2 breaks in 30 days: mark SUPERVISOR REVIEW at the start of the line. Above R$ 50 thousand, or customer with an order being picked now: mark URGENT and put it at the top of the table.

WHERE TO READ AND WRITE
Find the root folder \"Distributor Payment Promises Tess\" by its EXACT name, with trashed = false. If none has that exact name, answer \"FOLDER NOT FOUND: create the folder Distributor Payment Promises Tess in Drive\" and stop; never use a folder with a similar name. If there is more than one, stop and say so. Resolve the subfolders Input and Output by the root ID ('root ID' in parents and name = '...' and trashed = false), never by name across the whole Drive. Read every file in Input; a file READ-base-date.txt, if present, sets today's date. Empty Input folder: stop without writing anything.
Write the result, in the OUTPUT FORMAT, to a file PAYPROMISES_YYYY-MM-DD_HHhMM.md (current Brasília clock, never the base date) on disk with Python open().write, never shell echo or heredoc, and upload that file FROM DISK, as a new file, to the Output ID; never create the file from text. Check that it is in Output (parents). If the upload fails twice, answer \"WRITE ERROR\" and stop. Do not delete or move Input. Do not write to any other system.",

collector_glossary.mdknowledge base, with a sample to replace
Show content
# Glossary of the collectors' notes

| Abbreviation | Means |
|---|---|
| pay | will pay |
| bl, bls | open bill (boleto, the Brazilian bank payment slip) |
| dep | deposit |
| tmrw, today, thu, wed | date relative to contact_date |
| fin will check | the customer's finance team will review: no commitment |
| promised again | new promise, counts as a separate promise |
| disputes, damaged, exchange | commercial dispute |

# Reading rules
1. A promise needs a commitment to pay and a date. With no date and no commitment (e.g.: "fin will check") it is not a promise: it counts only in notes read.
2. AMBIGUOUS is the note that allows two dates or two amounts. Transcribe the excerpt.
3. A commercial dispute is not a promise: it goes to the DISPUTES block, outside the summary.
4. Promised amount: sum of the bills cited in open_bills.csv. With no bill and no amount cited, use all of the customer's open bills.
5. Deadline: the promised date plus 1 business day. Holidays: Nov 2 and Nov 20. Credit after the deadline: BROKEN, with the credit date in the detail.
6. A customer credit with no bill within the deadline: the promise is NOT RECONCILED, never KEPT, and the credit goes to the unidentified list.
7. SUMMARY: percentages over the identified promises. Promised amount without the AMBIGUOUS ones. Amount received on time only with credits of identified bills.
8. Collector break rate: broken divided by that collector's identified promises.

## Rules with no leeway
- A person's name cited in the note does not appear in any part of the output. When transcribing the excerpt, replace the name with [name removed]. Only the collector's name (collector column) may appear.
- A credit with no bill is never assigned to a promise, even with an amount equal to the promised one.
- When more than one mark applies, use the highest: URGENT prevails over SUPERVISOR REVIEW. Customer with 2 breaks in 30 days: all of that customer's broken lines carry the mark.

## Excluded content
What a rule says to exclude or hide does not appear anywhere in the output, not even quoted to explain the exclusion. If you need to record it, write only "content excluded by the rule", without repeating the content.

## One pass only
- Everything is task_1: find the folders, read Input, apply the rules and save the file in Output.
- Do not build a plan with separate steps (locate, read, classify, write, save). A 1-task plan.

Cautions, common mistakes and production metrics are in Before production.

Before production

Cautions

The Human AI does not decide on order holds or protests: it classifies and the analyst puts customers back in the queue. A receipt with no identified invoice is never assigned to a promise because the amount is close, because that hides duplicate payments and credit applied to the wrong customer; the line comes out as NOT RECONCILED. A note about a commercial dispute is not a promise and goes into a separate block. The log carries the names of customer contacts; in the output use only the customer_id.

Common mistakes

  • Treating an unanswered contact attempt ('called, no answer') as a promise, which inflates the base and drags down the kept rate.
  • Marking a promise as kept when any payment from the customer came in, even for another invoice.
  • Comparing the promised date with the date on the payment receipt instead of the reconciled credit date.
  • Measuring promise-keeping only by number of promises, ignoring the amount recovered.

Metrics

MetricRangeSource
Time between a missed promised date and the next contactfrom 9 days on average to 1 to 2 business daysestimate based on the described routine
Analyst hours on the Monday reconciliationfrom 4 hours to under 1 hour, including the checkestimate based on the described routine
Promised date accuracy in calibration90% or more of promises with the correct date, verified in calibrationestimate based on the described routine

Sample production output

Fictional sample. Promise reconciliation, week of 2026-08-24 to 2026-08-28. 132 notes read, 87 promises identified.

customer 30812 | collector Ana | note 08/25: 'pd fri 2 slips' | promise: 08/28, 2 invoices, R$ 6,420.00 | received: 08/28 R$ 6,420.00 | KEPT
customer 11205 | collector Caio | note 08/26: 'dep 27, rest on the 5th' | promise: 08/27, R$ 3,100.00 of R$ 7,800.00 | received: 08/27 R$ 3,100.00 | PARTIAL, balance of R$ 4,700.00 promised for 09/05
customer 4087 | collector Ana | note 08/24: 'will pay thursday' | promise: 08/27, R$ 1,980.00 | received: nothing by 08/31 | BROKEN, 4 days, back to the queue today
customer 27710 | collector Lia | note 08/27: 'finance will check' | no date | AMBIGUOUS, ask for a log entry with a date

SUMMARY: kept 52 (60%), partial 9, broken 21, ambiguous 5. Amount promised R$ 412 thousand, amount received on time R$ 238 thousand. Collector with the highest broken rate: Lia, 8 of 19.
